name: Alpha Centauri B
tagline: Toliman — the orange K1V companion waltzing with Rigil Kentaurus every 79.9 years.
history: Alpha Centauri B is the cooler, smaller half of the nearest binary to the Sun. At 0.9 solar masses it glows a warm orange — about half the Sun's luminosity — and swings around the barycenter with the brighter yellow G2V primary on a markedly eccentric 80-year orbit: the pair close to 11.4 AU at periastron and stretch to 35.6 AU at apastron. To the naked eye from Earth the two merge into a single point — the third-brightest star of the night sky — but telescopes split them into a classic double, and the system's proximity keeps it at the top of every exoplanet search list, including the ongoing hunt for a temperate world around A.
source: ESO eso0307; Yale Bright Star Catalogue; Stellarcatalog
